title: Relative Clauses in Sentences about Kerkennah Islands
summary: A reading and discussion task where learners identify relative clauses in sentences describing Kerkennah islands, classify them as defining or non-defining, and then complete Activity Book exercises.

title: Tourism and Environment: Exploring Pros and Cons with an Essay
summary: Learners read Basim's notes listing pros and cons of tourism for the environment, then compare them with his final essay discussing economic benefits and environmental awareness alongside negative impacts.

title: Why Are Holidays So Important? Reading and Matching Headings
summary: A group discussion and skimming activity based on a text explaining the importance of holidays, covering stress effects, the benefits of change, and why some people never leave work.

title: Unit 5 Round Up: Key Grammar and Vocabulary Revision
summary: A revision page summarising the language focus of Unit 5, including compound nouns, present perfect forms, past perfect, and relative clauses, each illustrated with examples for partner discussion.

title: Literature Focus: Pride and Prejudice and As You Like It
summary: A divider page introducing the Literature Focus section, listing the two literary works studied: Pride and Prejudice and As You Like It.

title: Pride and Prejudice: About the Author, the Book, and the Story
summary: Three matching paragraphs covering Jane Austen's life, the publication history of Pride and Prejudice, and an introduction to the Bennet family and Bingley's arrival in town.

title: Pride and Prejudice Story Summary and Vocabulary Glossary
summary: Continuation of the novel's summary describing the relationship between Elizabeth and Darcy at a ball, followed by a glossary of key vocabulary words including worsened, anonymously, delightful, and chaotic.

title: Reading the Opening Scene and the Story So Far Box
summary: Learners read a 'The story so far' summary of the novel's opening scene and answer a comprehension question about why the Bennets discuss the new arrival, then complete Activity Book exercises.
